All Classes and Interfaces

Class
Description
AccountMailer
Port that sends the e-mails of the account lifecycle.
AccountMailException
An account message could not be delivered.
AccountToken
A single-use token that proves the right to perform one account operation.
AccountTokenRepository
Port that stores single-use account tokens.
AuthenticationContextClass
Authentication context class references (acr) that this server reports and understands.
AuthenticationFactor
A way of authenticating, as registered by a feature.
Base32
Base32 encoding (RFC 4648) without padding, the form authenticator applications expect for a shared secret.
CertificateAlreadyBoundException
Thrown when a certificate is already bound to another account: one certificate belongs to one account only.
CertificateBinding
The binding of a client certificate to an account: the certificate is recognised by the SHA-256 fingerprint of its encoded form, never by its subject, which anyone can choose.
CertificateBindingRepository
Port that stores the client certificates bound to accounts.
CertificateNotFoundException
Thrown when an account has no bound certificate with the requested identifier.
ClientAlreadyExistsException
A client with that identifier is already registered.
ClientAssertionReplayRegistry
Port that remembers the identifiers (jti) of the client assertions already accepted, so an assertion cannot be presented twice.
ClientAssertionUse
One presentation of a client assertion: which client presented which JWT identifier, and until when the assertion is valid (after that instant the identifier no longer needs to be remembered).
ClientNotFoundException
No client is registered with that identifier.
ClientRegistration
An OAuth 2.1 client registered with the authorization server.
ClientRegistrationRepository
Port that stores registered clients.
CompromisedPasswordCheck
Port that tells whether a password is known to have leaked in a data breach.
CompromisedPasswordException
The chosen password is known to be compromised.
ExpiredLinkTokenPurger
Port that removes the expired magic-link tokens.
FactorStrength
How much an authentication factor proves on its own.
FederatedIdentity
An identity of an external provider linked to a local account: the account is reached by presenting the provider's stable subject, never by its e-mail address, which a provider may change.
FederatedIdentityAlreadyLinkedException
Thrown when an identity of an external provider is already linked to another account: one external identity belongs to one account only.
FederatedIdentityNotFoundException
Thrown when an account has no linked identity with the requested identifier.
FederatedIdentityRepository
Port that stores the identities of external providers linked to accounts.
FederatedLinkingPolicy
Rules of identity brokering: when an external identity may be tied to an account, and when it may be removed.
FederatedLoginRefusedException
Thrown when a sign-in through an external provider is refused: the provider did not vouch for the e-mail address, or the address belongs to an account whose own address was never verified.
GeneratedPasswordRepository
Port that remembers which accounts only hold a password the server generated and nobody knows: the accounts created by the first sign-in with an external provider.
IdentityProvider
External identity providers an account can be linked to.
ImplicitClientRefusedException
A client with the legacy implicit grant was submitted through the administration API: only the demo client seeded under the legacy-implicit profile may have that grant, so the implicit flow never reaches a deployment that did not opt in to it.
InvalidAccountTokenException
The presented account token is unknown, expired, already used or issued for another purpose.
InvalidCredentialsException
The username or the current password is wrong.
InvalidPasskeyLabelException
Thrown when the label given to a passkey is refused: blank, or longer than allowed once trimmed.
InvalidPasswordException
The chosen password breaks the PasswordPolicy.
InvalidTotpCodeException
Thrown when the code presented to confirm the enrolment of an authenticator app is wrong.
LastSignInMethodException
Thrown when removing a sign-in method would leave the account with none, so its owner could never sign in again.
MfaPolicy
The rule that decides when the factors of an authentication are enough, and when they are required.
OneTimeCode
A numeric one-time code that was issued to a user.
OneTimeCodeGenerator
Port that generates the numeric codes users type.
OneTimeCodeHasher
Port that hashes one-time codes so that only the hash is stored.
OneTimeCodeRepository
Port that stores the numeric one-time codes.
OttChannel
Channel through which a one-time token reaches the user.
OttDelivery
Port that delivers a one-time token to a destination through a channel.
OttDeliveryException
Thrown when a one-time token could not be delivered.
OttKind
Shape of a one-time token.
OttPolicy
The rules of one-time tokens: how long each kind lives, how long a code is and how many wrong submissions are tolerated.
OttPurpose
What a one-time token is used for.
Passkey
A passkey (WebAuthn credential) registered by a user.
PasskeyNotFoundException
Thrown when a user has no passkey with the requested identifier.
PasskeyRepository
Port that reads and manages the passkeys users registered.
PasswordHasher
Port that hashes and checks passwords.
PasswordPolicy
Password rules in the style of NIST SP 800-63B: a minimum and a maximum length, no composition rules (no required digits, symbols or upper-case letters) and a password that does not contain the username.
PasswordViolation
A rule of the PasswordPolicy that a candidate password breaks.
PhoneCountryResolver
Port that tells the country of a phone number.
PhoneNormalizer
Port that turns the phone number a user typed into E.164.
PhoneNumber
A phone number in E.164 format.
PhoneVerification
A pending verification of a phone number: the code that was sent to it, hashed, until the user types it.
PhoneVerificationRepository
Port that stores the pending phone verification of each user, with the code hashed.
Preconditions
Argument checks shared by the domain models.
ProviderTrust
How far a provider's own multi-factor authentication is trusted.
RecoveryCode
A single-use code that replaces the second factor when the authenticator is lost.
RecoveryCodeRepository
Port that stores the recovery codes of each user.
SecondFactorAttemptRepository
Port that keeps the failed second-factor attempts of each user, so that a lockout survives restarts and is shared by every instance of the server.
SecondFactorLockedException
Thrown when a second factor is attempted while the user's second factor is locked after too many failures.
SecondFactorLockout
The failed-attempt state of the second factor of one user.
SecretGenerator
Port that creates the shared secrets of TOTP credentials.
SecureRandomSecretGenerator
Creates 160-bit secrets, the length RFC 4226 recommends for HMAC-SHA1, from a SecureRandom.
SecurityEvent
An authentication event kept for audit.
SecurityEventRepository
Port that stores the audit trail of authentication events.
SecurityEventType
Kinds of authentication events that are recorded for audit.
SignedTokenLifetimes
Port that tells how long the tokens signed with the signing keys stay valid, so that a retired key stays published for as long as any token it signed can still be presented.
SignedTokenService
Port that issues and verifies signed, purpose-bound tokens.
SigningKey
An asymmetric key pair used to sign tokens.
SigningKeyGenerator
Port that generates new signing keys.
SigningKeyRepository
Port that stores signing keys.
SigningKeyStatus
Lifecycle state of a signing key.
SignInMethods
The ways an account can sign in with.
SignInMethodsLock
Port that serializes the removals of the sign-in methods of one account (unlinking an identity, unbinding a certificate), so that two concurrent removals cannot each count the other's method as remaining and together leave the account with no way to sign in.
SmsCostLedgerRepository
Port that keeps the ledger of what text messages cost, in the database so that a restart cannot reset a budget.
SmsCostPolicy
The rules that keep text messages from costing too much: the countries messages may go to, what a message costs in each and the budget per window and per day.
SmsDeliveryException
Thrown when a text message could not be sent.
SmsInbox
Port that lists the messages a development sender recorded instead of sending them.
SmsInboxEntry
A text message a development sender recorded instead of sending it, as the development inbox shows it.
SmsMessage
A text message to send.
SmsSender
Port that sends a text message through a gateway.
SmsSpendCap
A spending cap of text messages: what may be spent in a window that ends at the message being sent.
TokenGenerator
Port that creates random opaque tokens and hashes them for storage.
TotpAlgorithm
The time-based one-time password algorithm of RFC 6238 over HMAC-SHA1, with the parameters every authenticator application supports: 30 second steps and 6 digits.
TotpAlreadyEnabledException
Thrown when a user who already confirmed an authenticator app tries to enrol another one.
TotpCredential
The TOTP credential of one user.
TotpCredentialRepository
Port that stores the TOTP credential of each user.
TotpNotEnrolledException
Thrown when a user has no authenticator app being enrolled, so there is nothing to confirm.
TotpSecretCipher
Port that protects TOTP secrets at rest.
TotpUri
Builds the otpauth:// URI that authenticator applications read from a QR code to enrol a secret.
TrustedDevice
A browser that a user chose to trust, which lets it skip the second factor (never the first) until it expires.
TrustedDeviceRepository
Port that stores the devices users trust.
TrustedDeviceTokenSigner
Port that signs the value of the trusted-device cookie and checks that signature, so a value the server did not issue is rejected before anything is looked up.
UserAccount
A user that can sign in with a password.
UserAccountRepository
Port that provides the user accounts able to sign in with a password.
UserAuthorizationRepository
Port that removes the stored authorizations (and so the tokens) of users.
UserMfaSettingsRepository
Port that stores the multi-factor settings of a user account.
UserPhone
The verified phone number of a user.
UserPhoneRepository
Port that stores the verified phone number of each user.
VerifiedEmailLookup
Port that asks an external provider for the verified primary e-mail address of the user who just signed in, for a provider whose profile does not vouch for its e-mail address (GitHub).
